records.source: Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς ἐγὼ ὁ δέσμιος ἐν κυρίῳ ἀξίως περιπατῆσαι τῆς κλήσεως ἧς ἐκλήθητε, μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης καὶ πραΰτητος, μετὰ μακροθυμίας, ἀνεχόμενοι ἀλλήλων ἐν ἀγάπῃ, σπουδάζοντες τηρεῖν τὴν ἑνότητα τοῦ πνεύματος ἐν τῷ συνδέσμῳ τῆς εἰρήνης·
records.gloss: I urge therefore you, I the prisoner in [the] Lord, worthily to walk of the calling with which you were called, \v 2 with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, \v 3 being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of the peace;
pieces: So I, a prisoner for the Lord, appeal to you: live in a way that is worthy of God's call, the call that came to you.
Be humble and gentle in every way, and be patient, putting up with one another in love.
Spare no effort to keep the unity the Spirit gives, with peace as the bond that holds you together.

L.1: I therefore, the prisoner in [the] Lord, urge you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
L.2: with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
L.3: being eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

R.1: I am a prisoner because I belong to the Lord. So I beg you: live the kind of life that fits what God called you to be.
R.2: Always be humble and gentle. Be patient, and put up with each other because you love each other.
R.3: The Spirit has made you one. Work hard to keep it that way, and let peace hold you together.

decisions.choice: therefore: the life now urged follows from what God has done in chapters 1-3
decisions.reason: οὖν turns the letter from what God has done (chapters 1-3: chosen, raised with Christ, Jews and Gentiles made one body) to how those who have received it are to live (chapters 4-6).

decisions.choice: the prisoner in the Lord: in chains because he belongs to the Lord and serves him
alternatives: a prisoner of the Lord, held captive by him (in a figurative sense)
decisions.reason: Paul wrote as a prisoner (3:1; 6:20). "In the Lord" says why: his imprisonment is part of his service to Christ, not a mark against him, and it gives weight to his appeal.

decisions.choice: walk worthily of the calling: live in a way that matches God's call
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a common biblical picture for the way a person lives (2:2, 2:10; Colossians 1:10). The calling is God's call that made them his people (1:18; 4:4); their conduct is to fit it.

decisions.choice: the unity of the Spirit: the oneness the Spirit has created, which they are to keep
alternatives: a unity of human spirit or attitude
decisions.reason: They are not told to make unity but to keep it: the Spirit has already joined Jews and Gentiles into one body (2:18, 2:22). The bond that holds it is peace, the peace Christ made between them (2:14-17).

decisions.choice: worthy of God's call, the call that came to you; what God called you to be
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who calls (m3), which the Greek passive implies.

decisions.choice: The Spirit has made you one. Work hard to keep it that way
decisions.reason: Readable says first what the Spirit has done, then what they must do (m4).

records.heading: Keep the unity the Spirit gives

records.source: ἓν σῶμα καὶ ἓν πνεῦμα, καθὼς καὶ ἐκλήθητε ἐν μιᾷ ἐλπίδι τῆς κλήσεως ὑμῶν·
records.gloss: one body and one Spirit, just as also you were called in one hope of the calling of you;
pieces: There is one body and one Spirit, just as there is one hope that belongs to the call you received.

L.4: [There is] one body and one Spirit, just as you also were called in one hope of your calling;

R.4: There is only one body, the church, and there is only one Spirit. In the same way, when God called you, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave all of you one hope to share.

decisions.choice: one body: the church; one Spirit: the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: The body is the church, Christ's body (1:22-23; 2:16). The Spirit is the one Spirit through whom Jews and Gentiles both have access to the Father (2:18), the same Spirit as in verse 3.

decisions.choice: in one hope of your calling: the one hope that God's call brings
decisions.reason: The hope is what God called them to look forward to: the inheritance and the glory of 1:18. All share one hope, because all were called by the one God.

decisions.choice: there is: the verb is supplied
decisions.reason: Verses 4-6 are a list with no verb, perhaps drawn from words the churches already knew. The sense is a statement: there is one body, one Spirit, and so on.

decisions.choice: the church; when God called you, he gave
decisions.reason: Readable says who the body is (m1) and who called them.

records.source: εἷς κύριος, μία πίστις, ἓν βάπτισμα·
records.gloss: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;
pieces: There is one Lord, one faith, one baptism,

L.5: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;

R.5: There is one Lord, and there is one faith and one baptism.

decisions.choice: one Lord: Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Paul calls Jesus the one Lord beside the one God the Father (1 Corinthians 8:6), and verse 6 goes on to the Father.

decisions.choice: one faith: the one trust in Christ that all believers share
decisions.reason: Here faith is the trust in the one Lord that all of them have; verse 13 speaks of growing into "the unity of the faith". It may also include what is believed, since the two cannot be separated here.

decisions.choice: one baptism: the baptism every believer received in the name of Jesus
decisions.reason: There is one baptism, into the one Lord, for Jews and Gentiles alike (Galatians 3:27-28).

records.source: εἷς θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ πάντων, ὁ ἐπὶ πάντων καὶ διὰ πάντων καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν.
records.gloss: one God and Father of all, the [one] over all and through all and in all.
pieces: one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.

L.6: one God and Father of all, who [is] over all and through all and in all.

R.6: And there is one God, the Father of all. He rules over all, works through all, and is in all.

decisions.choice: all: everything God has made, with his people chiefly in view
decisions.reason: The Greek form can mean "all people" or "all things". God is Father of every family (3:14-15) and works all things (1:11), yet the list is about the church's unity, so believers are chiefly in view. The text keeps the open "all".

decisions.choice: over all, through all, in all: God rules everything, works through everything, and is present in everything
decisions.reason: The three phrases say that the one God is above all as ruler, active through all, and present in all. This is why there can be only one people of God.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in all"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "us" ("in us all"), and some "you". Important early manuscripts have only "in all". The added word narrows the phrase to believers.

decisions.choice: rules over all, works through all, and is in all
decisions.reason: Readable gives each short phrase a verb to say what God does (m2).

records.source: Ἑνὶ δὲ ἑκάστῳ ἡμῶν ἐδόθη ἡ χάρις κατὰ τὸ μέτρον τῆς δωρεᾶς τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: To one but each of us was given the grace according to the measure of the gift of the Christ.
pieces: But grace was given to each one of us, in the measure in which {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} gave it.

L.7: But to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of the gift of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.7: But {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has given grace to each one of us. He decided how much to give each of us.

decisions.choice: grace: God's free gift, here the gift that fits each believer for a part in the church's life
decisions.reason: Paul spoke of the grace given to him to make him a servant of the gospel (3:7-8). Each believer, not only apostles, has received grace in this sense, and verses 11-16 show what it is for.

decisions.choice: the measure of the gift of Christ: the amount Christ chose to give
decisions.reason: Christ is the giver (verses 8 and 11). Each one's gift is measured out by him, so no one has all of them and no one has none.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}".

decisions.choice: He decided how much to give each of us
decisions.reason: Readable explains "according to the measure of the gift" (m2).

records.heading: Gifts for building up the body

records.source: διὸ λέγει· Ἀναβὰς εἰς ὕψος ᾐχμαλώτευσεν αἰχμαλωσίαν, ἔδωκεν δόματα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
records.gloss: Therefore it says: Having gone up to height he took captive captivity, he gave gifts to the men.
pieces: That is why it says, "When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up on high, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led a band of captives, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave gifts to {{gender:people|men}}."

L.8: Therefore it says, "Having ascended on high, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led captivity captive; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave gifts to {{gender:people|men}}."

R.8: That is why Scripture says, "When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up to the highest place, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took many prisoners, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave gifts to {{gender:people|men}}."

decisions.choice: Psalm 68:19: God going up in victory; Paul reads "gave gifts" where the psalm says "received gifts"
decisions.reason: Psalm 68 pictures God as a victorious king going up to his holy mountain, leading captives and receiving gifts from people. Paul applies the verse to Christ's going up after his victory, and he has "gave gifts to people" where the Hebrew and the Greek Old Testament both have "received gifts". The psalm itself goes on to God giving to his people (Psalm 68:10-11, 68:36), and a later Aramaic paraphrase of the Psalms also reads "gave". Either way Paul's point is clear: the risen and exalted Christ gives gifts to his people, and verses 11-16 say what they are.

decisions.choice: it says: Scripture says
decisions.reason: The subject of λέγει is not named. Paul often introduces Scripture in this way (5:14); it means "Scripture says" or "God says in Scripture".

decisions.choice: led captivity captive: led a train of captives in triumph
alternatives: he set free those who were held captive
decisions.reason: "Captivity" stands for a group of captives, as in Judges 5:12. In the psalm they are the conquered enemies of God; for Paul they are likely the hostile powers Christ defeated (1:20-22; Colossians 2:15). Some have read them as those Christ set free from captivity, but the psalm's picture is of a conqueror's victory march.

decisions.choice: people: human beings, men and women
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώποις is the general word for human beings, and the gifts of verse 11 go to the church as a whole.

decisions.choice: went up; led a band of captives / took many prisoners
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain verbs for "ascended" and say what "led captivity captive" means (m3).

decisions.choice: Scripture says
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject that the Greek leaves out (m2).

records.source: τὸ δὲ Ἀνέβη τί ἐστιν εἰ μὴ ὅτι καὶ κατέβη εἰς τὰ κατώτερα μέρη τῆς γῆς;
records.gloss: The and "He went up" what is it if not that also he went down into the lower parts of the earth?
pieces: Now what does "He went up" mean, if not that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had also come down into the lower parts of the earth?

L.9: Now [this word] "He ascended", what is it, except that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also descended into the lower parts of the earth?

R.9: The words "He went up" must mean that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had first come down, into the lower parts of the earth.

decisions.choice: the lower parts of the earth: left open; most likely the earth itself, below heaven, or the realm of the dead
alternatives: the earth itself (Christ's coming as a man)
the realm of the dead (Christ's death and burial)
Christ's coming back by the Spirit
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean (1) the lower regions, that is, the earth, so that Christ came down from heaven to the earth when he became a man; (2) the lowest parts of the earth, the grave or the realm of the dead, so that Christ went down into death before he rose (Psalm 63:10; Romans 10:7); or (3) Christ coming down again by the Spirit after he went up, at Pentecost. The contrast with "far above all the heavens" (verse 10) fits either of the first two. The text keeps the phrase as it is.

decisions.choice: "He went up" implies that he first came down
decisions.reason: Paul takes one word of the psalm and draws out what it implies: one who goes up must have come down first. The going up is Christ's rise to the Father, after his death and resurrection (1:20).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "he also went down"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "first" ("he first went down"), which makes the order explicit. Important early manuscripts do not have it. A few early manuscripts also leave out the word "parts". The meaning is not changed.

decisions.choice: went up; come down
decisions.reason: Plain verbs for "ascended" and "descended", as in verse 8. Literal keeps the older words.

records.source: ὁ καταβὰς αὐτός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ ἀναβὰς ὑπεράνω πάντων τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἵνα πληρώσῃ τὰ πάντα.
records.gloss: The [one] having gone down himself is also the [one] having gone up far above all the heavens, so that he might fill the all things.
pieces: The one who came down is the very same one who went up, far above all the heavens, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might fill all things.

L.10: The one who descended is {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} also the one who ascended far above all the heavens, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might fill all things.

R.10: The one who came down is the same one who went up, higher than all the heavens. He did this so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would fill everything with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence and power.

decisions.choice: fill all things: fill the whole universe with his presence and rule
decisions.reason: Christ, raised far above every power (1:20-23), fills all things: his rule and presence reach everywhere. The church is his body, "the fullness of him who fills all in all" (1:23), and from his place over all he gives the gifts that follow.

decisions.choice: the one who went down is the same one who went up
decisions.reason: αὐτός stresses that it is one and the same person: the Christ who came down is the Christ who now reigns.

decisions.choice: fill everything with his presence and power
decisions.reason: Readable says what "fill" means here (m1).

records.source: καὶ αὐτὸς ἔδωκεν τοὺς μὲν ἀποστόλους, τοὺς δὲ προφήτας, τοὺς δὲ εὐαγγελιστάς, τοὺς δὲ ποιμένας καὶ διδασκάλους, πρὸς τὸν καταρτισμὸν τῶν ἁγίων εἰς ἔργον διακονίας, εἰς οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, μέχρι καταντήσωμεν οἱ πάντες εἰς τὴν ἑνότητα τῆς πίστεως καὶ τῆς ἐπιγνώσεως τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰς ἄνδρα τέλειον, εἰς μέτρον ἡλικίας τοῦ πληρώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἵνα μηκέτι ὦμεν νήπιοι, κλυδωνιζόμενοι καὶ περιφερόμενοι παντὶ ἀνέμῳ τῆς διδασκαλίας ἐν τῇ κυβείᾳ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐν πανουργίᾳ πρὸς τὴν μεθοδείαν τῆς πλάνης, ἀληθεύοντες δὲ ἐν ἀγάπῃ αὐξήσωμεν εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα, ὅς ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλή, Χριστός, ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα συναρμολογούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον διὰ πάσης ἁφῆς τῆς ἐπιχορηγίας κατ’ ἐνέργειαν ἐν μέτρῳ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου μέρους τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ σώματος ποιεῖται εἰς οἰκοδομὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ.
records.gloss: And he gave the [ones] on one hand apostles, the [ones] and prophets, the [ones] and evangelists, the [ones] and shepherds and teachers, \v 12 toward the equipping of the holy [ones] for work of service, for building up of the body of the Christ, \v 13 until we arrive the all at the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of the God, at man mature, at measure of stature of the fullness of the Christ, \v 14 so that no longer we may be infants, being tossed by waves and being carried around by every wind of the teaching in the dice-playing of the men in craftiness toward the scheming of the deceit, \v 15 being truthful but in love we may grow into him the all things, who is the head, Christ, \v 16 from whom all the body being joined together and being held together through every joint of the supply according to working in measure of one each part the growth of the body makes for building up of itself in love.
pieces: It was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who gave some to be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, and some shepherds and teachers.
He gave them to equip God's holy people for the work of serving, so that the body of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} would be built up,

until all of us arrive at the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God. Then we will be a mature {{gender:adult|man}}, grown to the full measure of the stature that belongs to the fullness of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
We will no longer be infants, thrown about by the waves and driven this way and that by each new wind of teaching, at the mercy of people who play tricks and cunningly scheme to lead others astray.
Instead, as we speak the truth in love, we must grow in every respect into {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the head, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
From {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the whole body is joined and held together by every ligament that supplies it. As each part does its own work, the body grows and builds itself up in love.

L.11: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} gave some [as] apostles, and some [as] prophets, and some [as] evangelists, and some [as] shepherds and teachers,
L.12: for the equipping of the holy [ones] for [the] work of service, for [the] building up of the body of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.13: until we all arrive at the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, at a mature {{gender:adult|man}}, at [the] measure of [the] stature of the fullness of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.14: so that we may no longer be infants, tossed by waves and carried around by every wind of teaching, by the trickery of {{gender:people|men}}, by craftiness in the scheming of deceit,
L.15: but speaking truth in love, we may grow into {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [in] all things, who is the head, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.16: from whom the whole body, being joined together and held together through every supporting ligament, according to [the] working in [the] measure of each single part, makes the growth of the body for [the] building up of itself in love.

R.11: He gave some people to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists who tell the good news, and some to be shepherds and teachers of God's people.
R.12: He gave them to prepare God's holy people to serve, so that the body of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the church, would grow strong.
R.13: This will go on until all of us are one in our faith and in knowing the Son of God. Then we will be grown up, like a mature {{gender:adult|man}}, and we will reach the full measure of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
R.14: Then we will no longer be like little children. We will not be like a small boat tossed by the waves, pushed one way and then another by every new teaching that blows along. We will not be fooled by people who use clever tricks to lead others the wrong way.
R.15: Instead, we will speak the truth with love, and we will grow up in every way, closer to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, who is the head of the body.
R.16: Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the whole body is joined and held together, and every joint helps supply what it needs. When each part does its own work, the body grows and builds itself up in love.

decisions.choice: he gave some as apostles...: the gifts of verse 8 are people
decisions.reason: αὐτὸς picks up "he gave gifts" from the psalm (verse 8): the gifts Christ gives his church are people given to serve it. The list names gifted people, not only their abilities.

decisions.choice: apostles, prophets, evangelists
decisions.reason: Apostles were those sent by the risen Christ with his authority (1:1). Prophets spoke messages given by God to the church; with the apostles they are the church's foundation (2:20; 3:5). Evangelists proclaimed the gospel, especially where it had not been heard (Acts 21:8; 2 Timothy 4:5).

decisions.choice: shepherds and teachers: one group with two closely joined tasks, or two closely linked groups
decisions.reason: The other names each have their own article (τοὺς), but one article covers both ποιμένας and διδασκάλους. This joins them closely: those who care for God's people as shepherds also teach them, though not every teacher need be a shepherd. Shepherding is the Bible's picture for leaders who care for God's people (Acts 20:28; 1 Peter 5:2).

decisions.choice: Christ gave these people to equip the saints for works of service, with the building up of the body as the goal
alternatives: three parallel purposes of the leaders: to equip the saints, to do the work of ministry, to build up the body
decisions.reason: The three phrases are not parallel. The first uses πρὸς, the next two εἰς: the leaders equip God's holy people, so that the people do the work of service, and so the body is built up. Some readings put a comma after "saints" and make three parallel tasks of the leaders: equipping the saints, doing the work of ministry, building up the body. The change of preposition, and verse 16, where every part does its work, favor the reading that gives the work of service to all God's people.

decisions.choice: equipping: preparing and making fit
decisions.reason: καταρτισμὸν comes from a verb used of mending nets (Mark 1:19) and of making something complete and ready for use. The leaders' task is to make God's people ready for their work.

decisions.choice: a mature man: the whole church grown to adulthood, not maleness
decisions.reason: ἄνδρα is the word for a grown man, chosen here because it is the opposite of "infants" in verse 14. The contrast is between childhood and full-grown maturity. It is one figure for the whole church together, not for each person alone.

decisions.choice: the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ: maturity measured by Christ in his fullness
decisions.reason: ἡλικίας can mean age or bodily height; either way the picture is of growing up. The standard is not a human one: the church is to grow until it matches the full measure of Christ.

decisions.choice: the unity of the faith: the oneness that comes from sharing one faith
decisions.reason: The faith here is the shared trust in Christ, as in verse 5, together with the knowledge of him. The unity of the Spirit already exists (verse 3); this unity is reached as the church grows.

decisions.choice: infants tossed by waves and every wind of teaching: unstable and easily led astray
decisions.reason: The picture is of a small boat at sea, thrown about by every change of wind. κυβείᾳ means dice-playing, and came to mean trickery and cheating; πανουργίᾳ is cunning, and μεθοδείαν scheming (the same word as "the schemes of the devil", 6:11).

decisions.choice: speaking the truth: being truthful in word and life
decisions.reason: ἀληθεύοντες means speaking the truth, and with it holding to the truth, in contrast to the deceit of verse 14. It is done in love.

decisions.choice: grow into him: grow toward Christ, the head, and become more fully joined to him
decisions.reason: The body grows up into its head: the church grows toward Christ and comes to match him more fully. "In all things" means in every way.

decisions.choice: the body's growth comes from Christ, through every part working
decisions.reason: Christ is the source of the growth ("from whom"). The body is fitted and held together by every ligament (ἁφῆς) that supplies it, as each part works. Colossians 2:19 uses the same picture.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article where the Greek has it.

decisions.choice: a mature {{gender:adult|man}}
decisions.reason: The figure is about adulthood, not being male (m6). "Adult" is the default; "man" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: shepherds
decisions.reason: The Greek word means shepherds. "Pastors" comes from the Latin word for shepherd, but it now names a church office and loses the picture.

decisions.choice: evangelists who tell the good news; the church
decisions.reason: Readable says what evangelists do (m2) and who the body is.

decisions.choice: like a small boat
decisions.reason: Readable names the picture behind "tossed by waves" (m9).

records.source: Τοῦτο οὖν λέγω καὶ μαρτύρομαι ἐν κυρίῳ, μηκέτι ὑμᾶς περιπατεῖν καθὼς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη περιπατεῖ ἐν ματαιότητι τοῦ νοὸς αὐτῶν, ἐσκοτωμένοι τῇ διανοίᾳ ὄντες, ἀπηλλοτριωμένοι τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ θεοῦ, διὰ τὴν ἄγνοιαν τὴν οὖσαν ἐν αὐτοῖς, διὰ τὴν πώρωσιν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν, οἵτινες ἀπηλγηκότες ἑαυτοὺς παρέδωκαν τῇ ἀσελγείᾳ εἰς ἐργασίαν ἀκαθαρσίας πάσης ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ.
records.gloss: This therefore I say and testify in [the] Lord, no longer you to walk as also the Gentiles walk in futility of the mind of them, \v 18 having been darkened in the understanding being, having been alienated from the life of the God, because of the ignorance the being in them, because of the hardness of the heart of them, \v 19 who having become callous themselves gave over to the sensuality for [the] working of impurity of all in greed.
pieces: So I tell you this, and insist on it in the Lord: you must no longer live as the Gentiles live, with their futile, empty thinking.
Their understanding is darkened, and they are cut off from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them, because their hearts have grown hard.
They have lost all feeling and have given themselves over to indecency, practicing every kind of impurity with an appetite that always wants more.

L.17: This, therefore, I say and testify in [the] Lord: [that] you no longer walk as the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their mind,
L.18: being darkened in [their] understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them, because of the hardness of their heart;
L.19: [they are people] who, having become callous, gave themselves over to sensuality, for the practice of every impurity, with greed.

R.17: So I tell you this, and I say it with the Lord's authority: do not live any longer like the Gentiles, the people who do not know God. Their thoughts are empty and lead nowhere.
R.18: Their minds are in the dark. They are far away from the life that God gives, because they do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and their hearts have become hard.
R.19: They no longer feel shame. They have given themselves over to shameless living. They do every kind of impure thing, and they always want more.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the nations who do not know God
decisions.reason: τὰ ἔθνη means the non-Jewish nations. The readers were Gentiles by birth (2:11; 3:1), but they now belong to God's people; here the word means those who still live without God (2:12).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "as the Gentiles also walk"
alternatives: "as the rest of the Gentiles walk"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "as the rest of the Gentiles walk", which counts the readers among the Gentiles. Important early manuscripts do not have "the rest".

decisions.choice: the futility of their mind: thinking that is empty and leads to nothing
decisions.reason: ματαιότητι is emptiness, what has no result or purpose. It is the word used of human thinking that has turned from God (Romans 1:21; 8:20).

decisions.choice: cut off from the life of God because of ignorance and hardness of heart
decisions.reason: The life of God is the life that God has and gives. They are shut out from it because they do not know God, and they do not know him because their hearts have grown hard. πώρωσιν means a hardening, as of skin or bone, that makes a person unable to feel or respond (Mark 3:5; Romans 11:25).

decisions.choice: callous, sensuality, greed
decisions.reason: ἀπηλγηκότες means having stopped feeling pain, past caring. ἀσελγείᾳ is open, shameless indecency without restraint. πλεονεξίᾳ is the craving to have more and more; it can include sexual greed, since it stands beside "impurity" (5:3; Colossians 3:5).

decisions.choice: cut off from the life of God; an appetite that always wants more
decisions.reason: Balanced uses plain words for "alienated" and "greed" (m4, m5).

decisions.choice: the people who do not know God; because they do not know him
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Gentiles are here (m1) and what their ignorance is (m4).

decisions.choice: I say it with the Lord's authority
decisions.reason: Readable says what "testify in the Lord" means: Paul speaks as one who belongs to the Lord and with his authority.

records.heading: Strip off the old self, put on the new

records.source: ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐχ οὕτως ἐμάθετε τὸν Χριστόν, εἴ γε αὐτὸν ἠκούσατε καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐδιδάχθητε, καθώς ἐστιν ἀλήθεια ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἀποθέσθαι ὑμᾶς κατὰ τὴν προτέραν ἀναστροφὴν τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν φθειρόμενον κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης, ἀνανεοῦσθαι δὲ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν, καὶ ἐνδύσασθαι τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν κατὰ θεὸν κτισθέντα ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ὁσιότητι τῆς ἀληθείας.
records.gloss: You but not so learned the Christ, \v 21 if indeed him you heard and in him you were taught, as is truth in the Jesus, \v 22 to put off you according to the former way of life the old man the [one] being corrupted according to the desires of the deceit, \v 23 to be renewed and in the spirit of the mind of you, \v 24 and to put on the new man the [one] according to God having been created in righteousness and holiness of the truth.
pieces: But that is not how you learned {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
You surely heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and were taught as people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, in keeping with the truth that is in Jesus.
You were taught to strip off the old self, the self of your former way of life, which is being ruined by its deceitful desires;
to be made new in the spirit of your minds;
and to put on the new self, created in God's likeness, in the righteousness and holiness that come from the truth.

L.20: But you did not learn the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} in this way,
L.21: if indeed you heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and were taught in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, as [the] truth is in Jesus:
L.22: that you put off, as concerns [your] former way of life, the old self, which is being corrupted according to the desires of deceit,
L.23: and that you be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
L.24: and put on the new self, created according to God in righteousness and holiness of the truth.

R.20: But that is not what you learned when you came to know {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
R.21: You heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and you were taught as people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. You learned the truth that is in Jesus.
R.22: You were taught to take off your old self, the way you used to live, like old clothes. That old self is being ruined by desires that trick you.
R.23: You were taught to let God make your thinking new,
R.24: and to put on the new self. God created this new self to be like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. It is righteous and holy, because it comes from the truth.

decisions.choice: learn Christ: come to know Christ himself, not only facts about him
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of learning a person. To learn Christ is to receive him as Lord and to be taught his way of life (Colossians 2:6-7); it rules out the way of life just described.

decisions.choice: if indeed: assuming, as is true, that you heard him
decisions.reason: εἴ γε does not doubt that they heard; it appeals to what they know (3:2). They heard Christ himself speaking through those who brought them the gospel, and were taught as people joined to him.

decisions.choice: as truth is in Jesus: the teaching they received matches the truth found in Jesus
decisions.reason: Paul uses the name Jesus alone, pointing to the man Jesus and his life: the truth is seen in him, and what they were taught agrees with it.

decisions.choice: put off, be renewed, put on: what they were taught, which they are to live out
alternatives: a past fact: you have put off the old self and put on the new
a command: put off the old self and put on the new
decisions.reason: The three verbs are infinitives depending on "you were taught" (verse 21): they give the content of the teaching. They can be read as stating what happened when the readers came to Christ (as Colossians 3:9-10 does: "you have put off the old self"), or as what they were taught to keep doing, with the force of a command. The first and last verbs are aorist, a decisive act; the middle one, "be renewed", is present, an ongoing process. Either way the teaching shapes how they must now live (verse 25).

decisions.choice: the old self: the person one was without Christ, ruled by the old way of life
decisions.reason: The old "man" is the whole person as he or she was before Christ, belonging to the old humanity (Romans 6:6; Colossians 3:9). It is "being corrupted": it is going to ruin, led by desires that deceive.

decisions.choice: the spirit of your mind: the inner attitude that directs the mind
alternatives: by the Spirit, in your mind
decisions.reason: Here πνεύματι most likely means the human spirit, the inner self that gives the mind its direction; God renews it (the verb is passive). Some read it as the Holy Spirit renewing the mind, but the phrase "of your mind" points to the human spirit.

decisions.choice: the new self, created according to God: made in God's likeness, Genesis 1:26-27
decisions.reason: κατὰ θεὸν means in the pattern of God, after his likeness. As in Colossians 3:10, the new self is a new creation in the image of its creator (2:10, 2:15).

decisions.choice: righteousness and holiness of the truth: righteousness and holiness that belong to the truth
decisions.reason: The phrase stands against "the desires of deceit" (verse 22). The new self's righteousness and holiness are real and come from the truth that is in Jesus (verse 21). It can also be read as "true righteousness and holiness".

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}".

decisions.choice: the old self; the new self
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the old man" and "the new man", but ἄνθρωπον here means a human being, of either sex (m5); "self" says this without a setting. Colossians 3:9-10 has the same words.

decisions.choice: You were taught to strip off... to be made new... to put on
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat "you were taught" so that the three verbs read as its content, as in the Greek (m4).

decisions.choice: like old clothes; let God make your thinking new
decisions.reason: Readable names the clothing picture in "put off" and "put on", and God as the one who renews (m6).

records.source: Διὸ ἀποθέμενοι τὸ ψεῦδος λαλεῖτε ἀλήθειαν ἕκαστος μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐσμὲν ἀλλήλων μέλη.
records.gloss: Therefore having put off the falsehood speak truth each with the neighbor of him, because we are of one another members.
pieces: So now that you have stripped off falsehood, each of you must tell your neighbor the truth, for we are members of one another.

L.25: Therefore, having put off falsehood, speak truth, each [one] with {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, for we are members of one another.

R.25: So stop telling lies. Each of you must tell the truth to the people around you, because we all belong to each other, like parts of one body.

decisions.choice: speak truth each with his neighbor: Zechariah 8:16
decisions.reason: Paul's words follow Zechariah 8:16 closely, where God tells his restored people to speak truth to one another. Paul does not mark it as a quotation; it is the command Israel was given, now given to the church. The neighbor here is above all the fellow believer, as the reason given shows.

decisions.choice: having put off falsehood: having taken off lying like old clothes
decisions.reason: ἀποθέμενοι is the same verb as "put off" in verse 22. Falsehood belongs to the old self they have stripped off; speaking truth belongs to the new self, created "in the holiness of the truth" (verse 24).

decisions.choice: members of one another: parts of one body, belonging to each other
decisions.reason: "Members" are the parts of a body (verse 16; Romans 12:5). To lie to a fellow believer is like one part of a body deceiving another.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: Each one, man or woman, is meant; "his" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: like parts of one body
decisions.reason: Readable explains "members" (m3).

records.heading: Living as members of one another

records.source: ὀργίζεσθε καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε· ὁ ἥλιος μὴ ἐπιδυέτω ἐπὶ παροργισμῷ ὑμῶν, μηδὲ δίδοτε τόπον τῷ διαβόλῳ.
records.gloss: Be angry and not sin; the sun not let set upon anger of you, \v 27 nor give place to the devil.
pieces: If you become angry, do not let it lead you into sin. Do not let the sunset find you still angry,
and do not give the devil an opening.

L.26: Be angry and do not sin; let the sun not set upon your anger,
L.27: nor give room to the devil.

R.26: When you are angry, do not let your anger lead you to sin. Deal with your anger before the day is over.
R.27: Do not give the devil any room to work.

decisions.choice: be angry and do not sin: Psalm 4:5, in the words of the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: The first words are exactly those of Psalm 4:5 in the Greek translation of the Old Testament. The Hebrew verb there means to tremble or be stirred, with fear or with anger.

decisions.choice: be angry and do not sin: anger is allowed for, but the command is not to sin in it
alternatives: a command to be angry at what is wrong
decisions.reason: The weight of the sentence is on "do not sin". Paul does not order the readers to be angry; he grants that anger will come and forbids letting it turn into sin. Verse 31 tells them to put away anger of the sinful kind.

decisions.choice: let the sun not set on your anger: do not keep your anger past the end of the day
decisions.reason: The day ended at sunset (compare Deuteronomy 24:15). Anger kept overnight becomes resentment. παροργισμῷ is anger that has been stirred up, a fit of anger.

decisions.choice: give place to the devil: give the devil an opportunity
decisions.reason: τόπον means a place, and so a chance or opening. Anger nursed and kept gives the devil a way in to do harm in the church.

decisions.choice: If you become angry / When you are angry, do not let it lead you into sin
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense of the command (m2), so that it is not read as an order to be angry. Literal keeps the form.

decisions.choice: Deal with your anger before the day is over
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of the sunset means (m3).

records.source: ὁ κλέπτων μηκέτι κλεπτέτω, μᾶλλον δὲ κοπιάτω ἐργαζόμενος ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσὶν τὸ ἀγαθόν, ἵνα ἔχῃ μεταδιδόναι τῷ χρείαν ἔχοντι.
records.gloss: The [one] stealing no longer let steal, rather but let toil working with the own hands the good, so that may have to share with the [one] need having.
pieces: Thieves must steal no more. Instead they must work hard, doing something good with their own hands, so that they have something to share with anyone in need.

L.28: Let the one who steals steal no longer, but rather let {{gender:them|him}} toil, working what is good with {{gender:their|his}} own hands, so that {{gender:they|he}} may have [something] to share with the one who has need.

R.28: If you have been stealing, stop. Work hard and do honest, useful work with your own hands. Then you will have something to give to people who are in need.

decisions.choice: the one who steals: anyone who has been stealing
decisions.reason: κλέπτων is a present participle: the one who has been in the habit of stealing. Paul speaks to anyone in the church, man or woman, whose old life included theft.

decisions.choice: toil, working what is good: hard, honest work
decisions.reason: κοπιάτω is to work to the point of weariness. "What is good" is useful, honest work in place of theft. Paul worked with his own hands too (1 Thessalonians 4:11; Acts 20:34-35).

decisions.choice: so that he may have something to share: the purpose of work is also giving
decisions.reason: The former thief, who took from others, is now to work so that he or she can give to others. The aim is not only to stop wrongdoing but to do its opposite.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}; {{gender:their|his}}; {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: Anyone is meant (m1); the masculine forms are the traditional alternative.

decisions.choice: Thieves... they
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the sentence in the plural, which means the same and needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: If you have been stealing, stop
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the reader directly, as the rest of the passage does. The sense is the same.

records.source: πᾶς λόγος σαπρὸς ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν μὴ ἐκπορευέσθω, ἀλλὰ εἴ τις ἀγαθὸς πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χρείας, ἵνα δῷ χάριν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν.
records.gloss: Every word rotten out of the mouth of you not let go out, but if any good for building up of the need, so that it may give grace to those hearing.
pieces: Let no rotten word pass your lips. Say only what is good, what builds up and meets the need of the moment, so that your words bring grace to those who hear them.

L.29: Let no rotten word go out of your mouth, but [only] whatever [is] good for building up [according to] the need, so that it may give grace to those who hear.

R.29: Do not let any ugly or harmful words come out of your mouth. Say only what is good and helpful, what makes others stronger when they need it. Then your words will be a gift of grace to those who hear them.

decisions.choice: rotten: foul, harmful and worthless
decisions.reason: σαπρὸς is used of rotten fruit and spoiled fish (Matthew 7:17; 13:48). Here it is speech that is foul or that does harm, the opposite of speech that builds up.

decisions.choice: for building up according to the need: what helps, fitted to what the moment calls for
decisions.reason: "Building up of the need" is a compressed phrase: speech that builds others up where there is a need, suited to the situation. "Building up" is the same word as in verses 12 and 16.

decisions.choice: give grace: be a gift and a blessing to the hearers
decisions.reason: χάριν here is a favor or benefit given. Good speech is a means by which God's grace reaches those who hear it.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "of the need"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "of the faith" in place of "of the need". The SBLGNT reading has much wider and earlier support.

decisions.choice: meets the need of the moment; when they need it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the compressed phrase (m2).

records.source: καὶ μὴ λυπεῖτε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἐσφραγίσθητε εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπολυτρώσεως.
records.gloss: And not grieve the Spirit the Holy of the God, in whom you were sealed for day of redemption.
pieces: And do not grieve God's Holy Spirit. It was with the Spirit that you were sealed, marked out for the day of redemption.

L.30: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for [the] day of redemption.

R.30: Do not make God's Holy Spirit sad. God gave you the Spirit as a seal, a mark that you belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The Spirit keeps you safe for the day when God will set you completely free.

decisions.choice: grieve the Holy Spirit: Isaiah 63:10
decisions.reason: Isaiah 63:10 says that Israel in the wilderness rebelled and grieved God's Holy Spirit. The sins of speech and anger in verses 25-31 do the same: they hurt the Spirit who has made the church one (verses 3-4). That the Spirit can be grieved shows that the Spirit is personal.

decisions.choice: sealed: marked as God's own and kept safe
decisions.reason: A seal marked ownership and protected what was sealed. Paul has already said they were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, the pledge of their inheritance (1:13-14). ἐν ᾧ here means "by" or "with" the Spirit.

decisions.choice: the day of redemption: the day God completes his people's release
decisions.reason: Believers already have redemption through Christ's blood (1:7), but its completion is still to come, on the day when God takes full possession of his people (1:14) and the body is set free (Romans 8:23).

decisions.choice: the day when God will set you completely free
decisions.reason: Readable says "set free" for redemption, as the rest of the letter does, and names God as the one who frees (m3).

decisions.choice: a seal, a mark that you belong to him; keeps you safe
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the seal means (m2), and repeats "the Spirit" rather than using a pronoun.

records.source: πᾶσα πικρία καὶ θυμὸς καὶ ὀργὴ καὶ κραυγὴ καὶ βλασφημία ἀρθήτω ἀφ’ ὑμῶν σὺν πάσῃ κακίᾳ.
records.gloss: All bitterness and rage and anger and shouting and slander let be removed from you with all malice.
pieces: Get rid of all bitterness, bursts of temper and anger, all shouting and slander, along with every kind of malice.

L.31: Let all bitterness and rage and anger and shouting and slander be taken away from you, with all malice.

R.31: Stop being bitter. Do not lose your temper or let anger rule you. Stop shouting at people and saying evil things about them. Get rid of every wish to hurt others.

decisions.choice: bitterness, rage, anger, shouting, slander
decisions.reason: πικρία is resentment that has gone sour. θυμὸς is an outburst of temper, ὀργὴ settled anger, κραυγὴ angry shouting, and βλασφημία slander, speech that wounds another's name. Colossians 3:8 has a similar list.

decisions.choice: malice: the wish to harm
decisions.reason: κακίᾳ is ill will, the wish to hurt, the root from which the other sins grow.

decisions.choice: bursts of temper
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 3:8, to tell rage from anger (m1).

decisions.choice: Stop being bitter... Get rid of every wish to hurt others
decisions.reason: Readable turns the list of nouns into plain commands, as Colossians 3:8 does.

records.source: γίνεσθε εἰς ἀλλήλους χρηστοί, εὔσπλαγχνοι, χαριζόμενοι ἑαυτοῖς καθὼς καὶ ὁ θεὸς ἐν Χριστῷ ἐχαρίσατο ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: Become to one another kind, compassionate, forgiving yourselves just as also the God in Christ forgave you.
pieces: Be kind to one another and full of compassion. Forgive each other freely, just as God has forgiven you in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.32: Become kind toward one another, compassionate, forgiving each other, just as God also in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} forgave you.

R.32: Be kind and loving to each other. Forgive each other, just as God forgave you because of what {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} did.

decisions.choice: compassionate: warm-hearted, quick to feel for others
decisions.reason: εὔσπλαγχνοι means having good inner parts; in the Bible the inner parts are where compassion is felt (Colossians 3:12).

decisions.choice: forgiving: giving freely, as God forgave
decisions.reason: χαριζόμενοι comes from the same root as χάρις: to forgive is to give freely what is not earned. The model is God's forgiveness (Colossians 3:13).

decisions.choice: in Christ: through what God did in Christ
decisions.reason: God forgave them in Christ: through Christ's death (1:7) and because they are joined to him.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "forgave you"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "forgave us". Both readings are early; the SBLGNT reads "you", which matches the commands addressed to "you". The meaning is not changed.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: because of what {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} did
decisions.reason: Readable explains "in Christ" (m3).
